Paragraph: When King Dasaratha was forced to fulfill Kaikeyi's boons to exile Rama, he was crushed by severe guilt, heartbreak, and emotional paralysis. Unable to bear the pain of betraying his beloved son, Dasaratha wept inconsolably in darkness, calling out to Rama until his heart gave way to grief.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Severe conflict of values, guilt over broken trust, heartbreak, and overwhelming stress leading to physical breakdown.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Dasaratha upholds truth (Satya) at terrible personal cost, choosing moral duty over personal desire while suffering intense heartbreak.
Outcome/Resolution: The tragedy underscores the painful reality of moral conflict and the somatic toll of unmanageable grief.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Satya-Palana (Upholding truth at immense personal cost)
Karma-Vipaka (Experiencing the tragic fruit of past errors)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Dasaratha sacrifices his life for truth, proving his commitment to honor even at the cost of personal survival.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Illustrates moral injury, intense guilt, and the physical breakdown caused by acute psychological distress.
